name: Robertson v. Methow Valley Citizens Council
summary: The Supreme Court held that NEPA imposes procedural but not substantive requirements—agencies must take a hard look at environmental consequences but are not required by NEPA to mitigate or prevent all harms identified.
significance: This case clarifies NEPA's procedural requirements, including what an adequate environmental impact statement must contain, and is frequently cited by both sides to define the 'hard look' standard agencies must meet.
